text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Russian newspapers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
KOMMERSANT DAILY
- U.S. astronaut Michael Foale may join his Russian crewmate in delicate repair work in the airless Spektr module.
- Former first deputy finance minister Andrei Vavilov, a key figure in Russia's worst financial scandal, denied all the charges.
- Former finance minister Alexander Livshits says he is the president's main economic expert.
- Big budget debtors will have to give their controlling shares to the government, the head of the State Tax Service is quoted as saying.
- Russia's elite team of professional cyclists is likely to fold because of financial problems.
SEVODNYA
- All the participants of the huge bank scandal, involving millions of dollars and some of the most powerful people in Russia, have spoken out. Now the prosecutors' office will have the last word.
- The Defence Ministry has recruited about 214,000 conscripts for the next two-year period of military service. About 18 percent of them are drug addicts and alcoholics.
- Russia's biggest confectionary firm, Red October, raised some $25 million in foreign investments last week through a private placement of its preferential shares.
NEZAVISIMAYA GAZETA
- Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin will try to convince Western businessmen to invest money in Russia's economy during his forthcoming visit to Brussels, scheduled to start on Thursday.
- President Boris Yeltsin has signed a decree aimed at strengthening his control over the activity of regional administrations.

- The story of the killing of Russia's last Tsar Nicholas II has too many unanswered questions to say when the remains of the tsar family, discovered in 1991 in Yekaterinburg, will be properly buried. The tsar, his wife, their four daughters and son were executed by the Bolsheviks on July 17, 1918.
IZVESTIA
- The financial pyramid MMM is being revived in a slightly different form, but the basic idea remains the same.
- Lack of information, money and expertise on the part of Russian traders complicate the situation of meat imports from Britain.
- The government owes more than 1.5 trillion roubles to gold producers.
- The government may invite commercial banks to finance fuel supplies to Russia's north because a lack of budgetary funds may lead to an energy crisis in the remote areas.
- The Tax Inspection is targetting not only prominent politicians and businessmen but also pop stars.
- The Mir orbital station crew is too worn out by a series of accidents to be prepared for a next 'unplanned' heroic deed, some experts say.
ROSSIISKAYA GAZETA
- A new programme has been prepared to improve the work of the Russian railway system and lower cargo tariffs.

- For decades the world knew about the only Soviet space launching site in Baikonur, whereas about 60 percent of domestic and 40 percent of the world launches had been carried out in Plisetsk in Russia's north.
- The newspaper publishes the text of Yeltsin's decree outlining the details of a new system of presidential control in the regions.
ROSSIISKIYE VESTI

- About 15,700 Russians have used a temporary direct telephone line to the presidential administration to complain about pensions arrears. Such a hot line linking people with the president should become a tradition.
MOSKOVSKY KOMSOMOLETS
- Despite summer holidays season an behind-the-scenes struggle within the government continues in Russia.
--Tatyana Ustinova, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520.
